newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IG Metall now hopeful of further wage deals.
newsitem.headline: German IG Metall now hopeful of further wage deals.

text.p: German metal and engineering sector trade union IG Metall said it was hopeful of more regional wage deals following the break-though agreement on sick pay reached overnight with employers in Lower Saxony.
"When employers participate as they did in Lower Saxony, there will be deals in other regions. That is my hope at least," a spokeswoman at IG Metall's headquarters in Frankfurt said by telephone.

After 13 hours of talks, negotiators for the engineering industry in the state of Lower Saxony said earlier they had agreed on a package to keep sick pay at 100 percent, thus not implementing an unpopular new law allowing a cut to 80 percent.

The package, which includes a wage increase of 1.5 percent from April, 1997 and a further 2.5-percent rise the next year, only applies to the 90,000 workers in Lower Saxony and was not intended as a "pilot deal" for the entire sector.

The IG Metall spokeswoman said this was the "first breakthrough" in the sector but stressed that following the collapse of national talks in October aimed at solving the dispute, it was still up to individual regional wage committees to find their own agreements.

The new law intended to cut sick pay, introduced in October as part of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's austerity package before the single European currency, has sparked protests involving hundreds of thousands of German workers.
